source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact original XML verse substring, including written/read notes, not a normalized substitute.
source.public_versification_note: Public and Hebrew verse numbering align throughout Exodus 12–18.

key_decisions.decision: Preserves divine hardening and glory through the defeated army, then marks return to narrative.
Keeps reported flight distinct from permitted departure and economic motive rooted in service.
Retains exact chosen force plus broader chariot force; officers does not claim a fixed third-rider arrangement.
Preserves both explicit divine agency and the raised-hand departure image, explained in a note.
Retains singular accusation to Moses even though his cry is not previously narrated.
Keeps divine hardening of wider Egyptians and repeated glory/military scope.
Retains both angel and pillar movements without defining their relation more precisely than the text.
Preserves difficult darkness/light juxtaposition without supplying separate effects for each camp as explicit Hebrew.
Follows pinned MT removal verb rather than emending to jammed; keeps Egyptian recognition of divine combat.
Preserves difficult flight toward the returning water, full strength and forceful shook image without changing direction to ease tension.
Retains total loss within the stated pursuing force and avoids an added claim about Pharaoh’s personal fate.
Retains hand idiom and visible dead bodies without softening the aftermath.
Keeps hand motif and fear alongside trust, with Moses explicitly servant rather than a competing divine object.
